reviewFindings: 1 (blocking) — fixed. `readPersistedRole` is the only place that knows an error came from the file's own bytes, so it is where the decision now lives: it throws `UnparseableRoleRecordError` for bytes that do not parse, answers `undefined` for ENOENT, and propagates every other failure unchanged. The startup catch tests for that one outcome and queues everything else — a listener answer that is not JSON, a schema miss, an EACCES, any transient error — and its line no longer names the role file except where the file is really at fault.

2 (blocking) — fixed in the same move. `transferRole` is best-effort: the queue stays set (it clears only after `restoreRole` resolves), the failure is reported once per failure run, and the heartbeat goes on to `syncRegisteredInterests()`. Doing it inside `transferRole` covers its second caller, `adoptHandoff`, as well. The doc comment says why the role may fail where the interests read may not: the role has a queue of its own and the session works without it; the interests read has no queue and needs the tick.
Thread PRRT_kwDORFy7ds6wAVT4, which the reviewer unresolved because its classification half was these two findings, is answered and resolved at this head. The other eight stay resolved.

packages/claude-envoy/tests/envoy-channel-handoff.test.ts — three behaviour rows: a non-JSON listener answer recovered, truncated local bytes never retried, an unreadable record not starving the interests
trickyParts: The `instanceof` test was sound for what it tested and wrong about where it was applied: `restoreRole` is a file read *and* a listener call, and the real client parses the listener's answer, so `SyntaxError` and `ZodError` reach the same catch from two origins. Moving the decision into `readPersistedRole` is what makes the test mean what it says; the fix removes a branch rather than adding one.
The startup catch sets `roleTransferFailureReported` itself when it queues, so the first heartbeat's retry does not repeat a line the operator has already read.
